elaine_fin: Hey team — AP flagged an invoice from Cumulus Analytics (Malta) that includes 18% Maltese VAT. Invoice attached: `INV-2026-045`. We don't have an EU VAT number on file. Should we pay and reclaim later or ask for corrected invoice without VAT?
ivan_ops: Do we have the vendor VAT ID recorded anywhere? If they supplied a VAT ID we might be able to reverse-charge, but we need a valid EU VAT for that.
julie_vendor: Hi Elaine — Julie from Cumulus. We did charge VAT by default because our billing system assumes EU B2B unless buyer provides VAT number. Our VAT reg is MT12345678. If Redwood can provide a Maltese/EU VAT number we can issue a reverse-charge invoice; otherwise we can issue a credit note and re-bill without VAT for export of services.
elaine_fin: Redwood HQ is US-based and we don't have an EU VAT registration. So the correct treatment for exported digital services to a non-EU business should be zero-rated / no VAT. Julie, can you issue a credit for the VAT and re-issue the invoice without VAT? We'll hold payment until corrected.
taxbot: FYI: For EU vendors selling to non-EU customers, supplier should not charge local VAT on exported services. See internal tax playbook: https://redwood.local/wiki/finance/tax-export-services (internal).
ivan_ops: Also flag: because this is a foreign vendor, we should request their W-8BEN-E to document non-US taxation for our records (keeps withholding documentation in order). Julie, can you provide a completed W-8BEN-E?
julie_vendor: We can supply a signed W-8BEN-E PDF. We confirm we will issue a credit for the 18% and resend an invoice without VAT. Expected turnaround ~2 business days. Apologies for the mix-up.
elaine_fin: Great — I'll mark invoice `on hold` and update the AP ticket. I'll request the credit + new invoice + W-8BEN-E from the vendor. If they insist on no credit, we'll escalate. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
taxbot: Logged: FIN-7842 vendor VAT credit requested, awaiting vendor docs.
